data.title: Daily Voice: Foreign inflows likely to sustain beyond November; gold offers better risk-reward than silver, says 360 ONE Asset's Mayur Patel
data.description:
Mayur Patel is the President and Fund Manager, Listed Equity at 360 ONE Asset
  • Expect foreign flows to sustain beyond November
  • Inflation remains a key risk
  • Risk-reward equation for gold turns more favourable
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Mayur Patel, President and Fund Manager – Listed Equity at 360 ONE Asset, expects foreign inflows to sustain beyond November. Foreign investor positioning remains near historic lows, while relative valuations have reset following two years of underperformance, leaving ample room for fresh allocations, he said in an interview with Moneycontrol.

According to him, inflation remains a key risk, with retail inflation at a two-year high of 6.09% and food inflation hovering near 9%. A more hawkish Reserve Bank of India (RBI) stance than currently anticipated by the market could weigh on valuations. Meanwhile, drought conditions in several states pose a threat to rural demand and credit growth, he said.

With a recovery expected to extend through 2027, the risk-reward equation for gold has turned more favourable, he believes.

"Gold is better placed than silver, as steady central bank buying provides a structural floor, while silver faces softening industrial demand and a possible supply surplus in 2027," Mayur Patel said.

Which sectors continue to offer attractive investment opportunities despite the sharp rally in recent months?

The rally is driven more by strong earnings, with September-quarter Nifty 500 profits, ex-oil-and-gas and metals, up 20%. Despite the bounce, we see good upside in private banks and urban NBFCs on strong credit growth and benign credit costs, while telecom offers reasonably valued growth.

We prefer bottom-up ideas in quick commerce, food delivery, hotels, auto ancillaries, power T&D, renewables manufacturing, pharma CDMO, hospitals and flexible offices.

Given the attractive valuations and pessimism around the sector has been overdone, have you started increasing your exposure to IT services stocks?

We remain underweight IT services, though positive on select bottom-up midcap ideas. Large-cap IT was oversold and has bounced sharply, but a structural re-rating looks difficult until business models transform.

The industry is in the early phase of AI-led revenue deflation, as clients seek to share productivity gains. Until new AI-led revenue streams scale up, we prefer to stay selective.

Do you expect more FIIs to return to Indian equities in the coming months, rather than their buying activity remaining limited to November?

Yes, we expect foreign flows to sustain beyond November. Record inflows of over Rs 1 lakh crore reflect a meaningful shift, as crude has eased from its October peak, the West Asia conflict is seeing hopes of resolution and September quarter earnings were strong. Foreign positioning remains near historic lows and relative valuations have reset after two years of underperformance, leaving ample room for allocation.

With India's data centre opportunity remaining a compelling long-term investment theme, which sectors would you prefer to gain exposure to this opportunity?

We prefer the enabling ecosystem over operators. Data centres are highly power-intensive, making power T&D, including transformers, cables and conductors, a key beneficiary, alongside renewable energy. Switchgear, backup power and cooling systems should see strong demand, while electronics manufacturing benefits from server and hardware localisation.

What are the key risks that investors should monitor in the coming months, and which factors could potentially derail the ongoing market rally?

Inflation is the key risk, with retail inflation at a two-year high of 6.09% and food inflation near 9%. A more hawkish RBI than market expectations could weigh on valuations. Drought in several states threatens rural demand and credit, while the sharp fall in gold prices could pressure gold lenders. Globally, elevated US yields and renewed West Asia tensions lifting crude remain critical risks.

Is this an opportune time to buy gold and silver following their sharp correction from the record highs recorded in January this year?

The correction has made valuations in precious metals more reasonable. Gold is more than a third below its January peak and silver nearly two-thirds lower, driven by Fed hike expectations, a stronger dollar and speculative liquidation rather than weaker fundamentals.

With a recovery expected through 2027, the risk-reward has turned more favourable. Gold is better placed than silver, as steady central bank buying provides a structural floor, while silver faces softening industrial demand and a possible supply surplus in 2027.

Do you believe the AI investment narrative is gradually shifting from chips to code and now to credit?

The narrative has evolved from chipmakers to software and applications, and now to financing this massive build-out. With data centre capex expected to exceed hyperscalers' operating cash flows, borrowing is rising, and investors are questioning returns. India, with limited direct AI exposure, becomes an attractive diversification play, while its cost advantage in building data centres opens a long-term opportunity.

data.title: Diaper maker Swara Baby Products to open Rs 800-crore IPO on Dec 2; sets price band at Rs 105-111
data.description:
Swara Baby Products IPO News
  • Swara Baby Products to open Rs 800-crore IPO on December 2
  • IPO Mix: Fresh issue of Rs 500 crore, OFS of Rs 300 crore
  • Swara Baby Products to debut on the stock exchanges on December 9
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Diapers and sanitary napkins manufacturer Swara Baby Products, promoted by Alok Birla and FirstCry parent Brainbees Solutions, is set to tap the capital markets with its maiden public offering worth Rs 800 crore, which will open for subscription on December 2.

The price band for the offer has been fixed at Rs 105-111 per share, valuing the company at Rs 3,211.5 crore at the upper end of the price band.

Of the total issue size, the company plans to raise Rs 500 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, while promoters Brainbees Solutions and Anadya Bon Merchari LLP will each offload shares worth Rs 150 crore through an offer for sale (OFS).

The OFS component has been reduced to Rs 300 crore from the earlier proposed Rs 500 crore, bringing down the overall IPO size to Rs 800 crore from Rs 1,000 crore envisaged in the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed in July 2026. SEBI cleared the company's IPO papers in October 2026.

The IPO anchor book will open for institutional investors on December 1, a day ahead of the public issue. The issue will close on December 4.

Related Stories

  • India draws $31 billion in climate funding since 2021, but investment remains concentrated: BCG-IVCA...
  • Supreme Universal launches 131-home tower at Chembur project in Mumbai
  • Data exclusivity will delay cheaper generics and hurt patients, says Biswajit Dhar

Swara Baby Products, a contract manufacturer of baby diapers, will finalise the share allotment on December 7, while its shares are scheduled to debut on the stock exchanges on December 9.

The company has reserved equity shares worth Rs 1.25 crore for its employees, who will be offered shares at a discount of Rs 10 per share to the final issue price.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Of the net public issue, excluding the employee reservation, 50 percent has been reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 15 percent for non-institutional investors (NIIs) and 35 percent for retail individual investors.

Business operations

Swara Baby Products claims to be India's largest contract manufacturer of baby and adult diapers, with estimated market shares of approximately 38 percent and 36 percent, respectively, in FY26.

Besides contract manufacturing, the company also manufactures and markets its own brands, including Cuddles in the baby diaper segment and Shields in the adult diaper category. These products are sold through online commerce platforms and modern trade channels.

The baby diaper segment contributed 79 percent of the company's revenue in FY26, followed by adult diapers at 16 percent, while the sanitary napkins business accounted for nearly 3 percent of the topline.

The company reported an 18.5 percent year-on-year growth in profit to Rs 95.6 crore and a 23.4 percent increase in revenue to Rs 1,163.9 crore in the financial year ended March 2026. For the quarter ended June 2026, it posted a profit of Rs 16.6 crore on revenue of Rs 322.8 crore.

Utilisation of IPO proceeds

Swara Baby Products plans to utilise Rs 198.2 crore from the net fresh issue proceeds towards setting up a new manufacturing facility in Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh. Another Rs 127.5 crore will be used for debt repayment, while the remaining proceeds will be allocated towards inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

As of June 2026, the company operated 20 manufacturing lines, comprising 12 lines for baby diapers, four for adult incontinence products and period panties, and four for sanitary napkins and panty liners.

Its manufacturing facilities have an annual production capacity of approximately 266 crore baby diapers, 25.3 crore adult diapers and period panties, and 75.6 crore sanitary napkins and panty liners.

JM Financial and Avendus Capital have been appointed as the merchant bankers to manage the Swara Baby Products IPO.

data.title: AI risk sets dollar for longest winning run since 2024
data.description:
The greenback has strengthened against all of its Group-of-10 peers, including the Japanese yen and the Swiss franc.
  • Dollar heads for longest winning streak in two years.
  • AI trade rupture and rate hikes drive safe-haven demand.
  • Traders price in further interest rate hikes by the Fed.
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

The dollar is poised for its longest monthly winning streak in two years as a rupture in the artificial intelligence trade and rising interest rates spur demand for safe-haven assets.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index is up 1.8% in November, putting it on track for a third straight month of gains. The greenback has strengthened against all of its Group-of-10 peers, including the Japanese yen and the Swiss franc.

A slump in technology stocks, coupled with robust economic growth and elevated inflation, propelled the dollar higher over the past three months. The greenback held near its strongest level since April 2025 in early Asian trading after jumping in pre-holiday US hours on Wednesday, as the Nasdaq 100 index briefly plunged into a bear market and a measure of underlying inflation hit the highest since 2023.

“It’s a pretty good dollar storm,” said Steven Englander, co-head of FX research and North America macro strategy at Standard Chartered.

Market repricing for a more hawkish Federal Reserve also supported the dollar this month, according to Sarah Ying, CIBC’s head of FX strategy.

Traders are fully pricing a 25 basis point interest rate hike next month for the Fed, and are betting on the possibility of two additional increases by the middle of next year. Policymakers have been flagging the need for more tightening, with some calling for lifting rates at successive meetings, while others are open to the possibility of raising by more than the usual quarter percentage point in December.

Some Wall Street strategists expect the dollar rally to extend into 2027, pointing to the very AI spending binge that’s making stock markets jittery as a driver of US economic growth and capital flows. The greenback has benefited from overseas investors converting local currencies to buy shares of US companies that use the tech.

“The US economy is booming and inflation is still moving away from the target,” said Win Thin, chief economist at Bank of Nassau 1982. “The Fed needs to hike rates to help cool the economy, perhaps in both December and January. That’s dollar positive.”

The dollar’s latest surge has won over short-dated options traders, but conviction further out has weakened over the past two months. The divergence suggests investors are positioning for dollar strength into early 2027 while becoming less willing to extend bullish bets much further.

Dollar’s Long-Term Volatility Signals Fading Optimism | Spot and options markets diverge since early October

The latest equities sell-off has raised concerns about the longevity of the AI boom, fueling sharp swings in global markets. In such an environment, the dollar has become “the haven of choice,” according to Goldman Sachs, while MUFG believes that the prospect of higher rates is also helping the currency.

“Weakness in the US equity market is taking place at a time when there is building evidence of strengthening cyclical growth momentum in the US, which is encouraging a stronger US dollar as a safe haven play,” said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG.

“The strength of the US economy supports the view of investors that returns are likely to remain higher in the US even if they are currently being challenged by the recent sell-off in US assets,” he said.

data.title: SEBI bars Le Lavoir, chairman and 13 others over alleged price manipulation, fund diversion, action before lock in expiry
data.description:
• SEBI bars Le Lavoir chairman Ashok Dilipkumar Jain from markets.
  • Order cites prima facie evidence of price manipulation and fraud.
  • SEBI also restrains Le Lavoir from raising any further capital.
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has barred Ashok Dilipkumar Jain, chairman of BSE-listed laundry services firm Le Lavoir Ltd, from accessing the securities market, citing prima facie evidence of alleged price manipulation, fund diversion and a scheme involving preferential warrants.

In an interim ex-parte order, the regulator also prohibited Le Lavoir from raising further capital and restrained 13 other entities and individuals from dealing in the company's shares until further orders. The action comes ahead of the November 29 expiry of the lock-in period for certain holdings, with SEBI apprehending that Jain and connected entities could dispose of their shares after the restriction ends.

The directions follow SEBI's examination of trading activity, WhatsApp communications, preferential allotment of warrants and subsequent movement of funds raised by the company.

SEBI said WhatsApp messages exchanged between Jain and Surendra Jain, promoter and director of Sunshine Capital Ltd, retrieved from a device seized during searches on December 5-6, 2024, contained discussions on Le Lavoir's shares, price targets, recommendations to buy the scrip and forthcoming corporate announcements.

The communications also referred to proposed corporate developments, including an increase in authorised share capital, and suggested the stock could rise substantially, with one message referring to a potential increase of 'Minimum 3X from the current prices.

Related Stories

  • APL Apollo’s minority shareholders will 'foot the bill' in Tata Steel deal: IiAS suggests Sebi sho...
  • Grey market premium is akin to betting, SEBI seeks to choke revenue incentives for such platforms
  • Adani firms plan public bond sale to raise Rs 2,000 crore

The regulator said these communications, along with the trading pattern and other material examined, prima facie indicated an intention to manipulate the scrip.

Also read: SEBI may ease SIF norms further, consider giving fund managers more flexibility

SEBI Whole Time Member Kamlesh Chandra Varshney, in his interim order, noted, “there is possibility of disposal of the shares upon expiry of the lock-in period, which presents a specific and time-sensitive concern. The alleged trading pattern, the substantial shareholding and the other circumstances discussed above warrant consideration of interim measures to prevent any action which may prejudice investors or frustrate the ongoing examination”.

Preferential allotment largely to connected entities

Jain joined Le Lavoir as chairman and non-executive director on November 19, 2024. The company subsequently proposed issuing 37.5 lakh convertible warrants at Rs 264.75 apiece, worth Rs 99.28 crore. The issue was scaled down, with 15.81 lakh warrants allotted to 25 investors in October 2025, raising around Rs 10.46 crore as initial subscription money.

SEBI alleged Jain, his wife and daughter received 8.78 lakh warrants. Allottees connected with Jain accounted for 13.47 lakh warrants, or 85.24 percent of the allotment.

Subscription money allegedly funded by Jain

SEBI's examination of bank statements of certain preferential allottees indicated that their subscription amounts were allegedly funded directly or indirectly by Jain or entities connected with him.

Sonali Abhaykumar Parmar, allotted 60,000 warrants, received Rs 40 lakh from Jain and his wife through Kirti Dilipkumar Jain, identified as Jain's sister, to fund her Rs 39.71 lakh initial subscription. Parmar subsequently paid the amount to Le Lavoir.

V P Jaware Gowda, allotted 78,000 warrants, received Rs 31.38 lakh from Sheeba Swapna, an entity/person connected with Jain, which was transferred to Le Lavoir within minutes. This represented around 60.79 percent of his initial subscription amount.

SEBI noted that Jain, his family members and Parmar accounted for around Rs 6.21 crore, or 59.37 percent of the total initial subscription amount received by Le Lavoir.

Proceeds routed to connected entities

SEBI flagged transfers involving Ghantiram Foods, Shree Vrajendra Foods and Ghura Industries, alleging funds moved through multiple entities before reaching Jain. It questioned a Rs 2.61 crore loan repayment to Dhanashree Electronics, noting no corresponding loan receipt in FY26 bank statements. Separately, Rs 1.55 crore was advanced to Ghura Industries, with portions subsequently routed through other entities.

Other concerns

SEBI flagged the discontinuation of arrangements with Hotel Fariyas and Hotel Tunga, whose subsequent developments were allegedly not disclosed to stock exchanges.

The regulator also said certain traders connected with Jain allegedly contributed to price increases through small trades, including single-share first trades above the previous day's closing price. It referred to earlier proceedings involving Jain and Darjeeling Industries Ltd.

The findings are prima facie observations in an ex-parte interim order. The noticees have been given 21 days to submit replies and seek a hearing.

data.title: Bitcoin tops $60,000 as risk assets rise in holiday trading
data.description:
Bitcoin

Bitcoin rose above the $60,000 mark on Thursday as risky assets tracked a rebound in tech equities, pushing crypto markets higher as they head into a period of thin holiday trading.

The largest cryptocurrency rose as much as 2.2% during the Asia session before paring some of those gains, changing hands at around $60,500 in New York trading. Other tokens including Ether and XRP also rose.

Bitcoin has lost more than a fifth of its value this month, putting it on course for its biggest monthly decline since a crypto-market meltdown more than four years ago. The sector has struggled to regain investor confidence amid a string of high-profile hacks, rising macroeconomic pressure and regulatory uncertainty following the US midterm elections.

“The rebound has improved the tape,” analysts at Marex wrote in a note Thursday. “It has not repaired the underlying demand picture.”

A set of US exchange-traded funds tracking the price of Bitcoin recorded $453 million in outflows on Wednesday, taking the group’s outflows over the past month above $5 billion. The products launched to great fanfare in January 2024, but performance has faltered under dampened demand for the underlying asset.

“With ETF selling still running at a heavy pace, Bitcoin may have found some short-term breathing room, but there is a real risk that the sellers return once the holiday dust settles, leaving the recent lows back in sight,” said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG.

Amagi Media Labs shares also witnessed buying interest, gaining 2.06 percent to Rs 582.8 and trading well above all their key moving averages.

Schaeffler Schweinfurt Beteiligungs GmbH sold 1.01 crore equity shares, representing 6.5 percent of the company's paid-up equity, in Schaeffler India for Rs 3,548.8 crore. The shares were sold from its 74.13 percent stake in the company.

Several global and domestic institutional investors acquired the shares sold by the promoter entity at Rs 3,493 apiece. ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund emerged as the largest buyer, picking up 17.15 lakh shares for Rs 599.05 crore, followed by SBI Mutual Fund, which acquired 14.4 lakh shares for Rs 502.99 crore. Mirae Asset Mutual Fund purchased another 10 lakh shares for Rs 349.3 crore.

Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC, Ashoka India, Goldman Sachs Bank Europe, HDFC Standard Life Insurance Company, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore, Nippon India Mutual Fund, Societe Generale, Sundaram Mutual Fund, Tata Mutual Fund, UTI AMC, WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund, Edelweiss Mutual Fund and National Pension System (NPS) Trust, among others, also participated in the block deals in Schaeffler India.

Norwest Venture Partners offloads over 2% stake in Amagi Media Labs

Meanwhile, Norwest Venture Partners X Mauritius offloaded 47.37 lakh equity shares, representing 2.15 percent of the paid-up equity, in Amagi Media Labs for Rs 262.44 crore.

On the buying side, Long Term Equity Fund, Old Bridge Capital Management and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund acquired the shares sold by Norwest Venture Partners at Rs 554 apiece.

Among the buyers, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund acquired 33.27 lakh additional shares, equivalent to a 1.51 percent stake, for Rs 184.32 crore. Long Term Equity Fund purchased 6.45 lakh shares for Rs 35.73 crore, while Old Bridge Capital Management - All Cap Strategy picked up 7.65 lakh shares for Rs 42.38 crore.

Alkem Laboratories promoter sells Rs 182 crore worth of shares to four institutional investors

Meanwhile, Alkem Laboratories promoter Seema Singh offloaded 3.58 lakh equity shares, representing 0.3 percent of the company's paid-up equity, for Rs 182.03 crore. The shares were sold from her holding of 25.79 lakh shares, equivalent to a 2.16 percent stake, as of September 2026.

Four institutional investors, comprising three asset management companies and an insurance firm, acquired the shares sold by the promoter at Rs 5,075 apiece.

ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Nippon India Mutual Fund and HDFC AMC each acquired 95,000 equity shares in Alkem Laboratories for Rs 48.21 crore apiece, while Bajaj Life Insurance purchased 73,695 shares for Rs 37.4 crore.

In terms of stock market reaction, Alkem Laboratories shares gained 0.34 percent to close at Rs 5,156.5.

data.description:

  • Fairfax Financial Holdings emerged as the successful bidder.
  • The government and LIC plan to sell a 60.72 percent stake.

The proposed strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank has entered a crucial stage, with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) examining the credentials of the successful bidder, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Dr Arunish Chawla said at Moneycontrol FiDEX 2.0 in Mumbai.

Prem Watsa-led Fairfax Financial Holdings has emerged as the successful bidder for the bank.

Asked how confident the government was that the transaction would go through, Chawla compared the disinvestment process to a four-lap relay race, saying the first two stages had been completed and the baton had now been handed over to the RBI.

"It's like a relay race. If you have seen how a 4 into 400 metre relay race is run, it has four laps. The first lap was expression of interest, (between) 2022 and 2024 it has been completed. The second lap was RFP which has been completed," Chawla said.

"The third lap we have handed over the baton to the RBI. RBI is a highly respected regulator. It knows its job. Let it complete the third lap and we will go forward," he added.

Related Stories

  • Bank unions call nationwide strike on December 3 against IDBI Bank stake sale to Fairfax
  • IIFL Capital’s investment banking head Nipun Goel steps down
  • Govt, LIC to become public shareholders in IDBI Bank after strategic sale: DIPAM Secretary

The remarks come after the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved the sale of a 60.72 percent stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,878 crore on October 14.

Also read: SEBI may ease SIF norms further, consider giving fund managers more flexibility

The proposed transaction involves the government's 30.48 percent stake and Life Insurance Corporation of India's (LIC) 30.24 percent holding in the bank. Following the sale, the government and LIC will retain stakes of 15 percent and 19 percent, respectively.

The RBI's assessment of the successful bidder is a key regulatory milestone before the transaction can proceed towards completion. Fairfax will have to undergo the RBI's fit-and-proper assessment and meet applicable regulatory requirements before the acquisition can be completed.

The IDBI Bank acquisition will also require Fairfax to take a call on its existing investment in CSB Bank, where it holds around 40 percent stake. Earlier, Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa told Moneycontrol that the RBI had given the group 2 years to decide whether to merge the Kerala-based lender with IDBI Bank or sell its stake in CSB Bank. The group is expected to take a decision after completing the IDBI Bank acquisition.

Once the necessary regulatory clearances are obtained, the transaction can move to the subsequent stages, including execution of the share purchase agreement and completion of the stake sale. The successful bidder will also have to make an open offer to minority shareholders under applicable regulations.

The IDBI Bank strategic disinvestment process was initiated in October 2022. The transaction is one of the government's biggest planned strategic stake sales in the banking sector.

data.title: Grey market premium is akin to betting, SEBI seeks to choke revenue incentives for such platforms
data.description:
• SEBI views IPO grey market premium as akin to betting.
  • Regulator aims to reduce GMP influence on investors.
  • SEBI warns intermediaries against displaying GMP.
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) views the grey market premium (GMP) for IPOs as akin to betting and is seeking to reduce its influence on investors' decisions by choking the revenue incentives for platforms that display such prices, a senior official said at Moneycontrol FiDEX 2.0.

The regulator may not be able to stop grey market premium transactions, which take place outside the formal market structure, but it can ensure that regulated entities do not promote or lend credibility to the practice, Jeevan Sonparote, Executive Director at the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), said.

“What we are trying to do is stifle the revenue generation from this, from the securities market to these entities so that they do not have any further incentive to provide this grey market premium,” Sonparote said.

“I don't think we can stop the grey market premium but definitely we can try to strangle it to make it a minuscule part of an investment decision for the investor and that is our attempt,” he added.

The remarks come after SEBI issued a cautionary advisory asking brokers, merchant bankers, entities associated with registered intermediaries and their agents to stay away from displaying grey market premiums.

Related Stories

  • Adani firms plan public bond sale to raise Rs 2,000 crore
  • SEBI appoints Santosh Kumar Shukla as Executive Director in legal department
  • SEBI may ease SIF norms further, consider giving fund managers more flexibility

Also read: SEBI eases KYC onboarding makes mobile verification optional in certain cases, mandates of delinking inactive accounts

Sonparote said the grey market is an unregulated space where there is no assurance that transactions are actually taking place, no investor protection or risk management mechanism, and no legally enforceable contract.

“Is real trading happening? Nobody knows. If it's happening, it's illegal. Because you are supposed to do trading only on the exchange. There's no guarantee. There is no risk management for the investor. This is not a contract under the Contracts Act,” he said.

According to Sonparote, grey market premium has gained traction because investors are increasingly focused on the listing-day gains rather than the company's long-term prospects.

“Why somebody needs a grey market premium? Because he's looking at the first-day pop. But is that what the investor should be looking at? Is it not that the investor should look at the history of the company, what the prospects of the company are and whether he should stick with this company, how this company will do in the next three to five years,” he said.

He said the growing reliance on GMP reflects a mismatch between the regulator's expectations of investors and the behaviour of those participating in the IPO market.

“If that is the investor that somebody wants to cater to, I think then there is a distinct mismatch between what we expect the investor and what the investor expects from this particular market. That really is not investing, it is only betting,” Sonparote said.

The regulator is also concerned that the practice has become normalised, with platforms displaying GMP alongside advertisements of brokers and merchant bankers, creating a commercial incentive to promote the grey market.

SEBI's regulatory framework also restricts registered intermediaries and their agents from associating with entities that make claims about returns or performance without regulatory permission. The framework provides for permitted platforms subject to safeguards, but GMP-based return claims do not currently have a certification mechanism under the PAARVA framework, Sonparote said.

The regulator's latest advisory is aimed at preventing intermediaries from associating with such platforms and helping investors avoid being influenced by purported listing gains.
